findings.summary: Work submitted is for a different node entirely (canary-retry-proof / echo utility), not job-state-consistency. The patch.diff, decision.md, and result-summary.md all describe implementing an echo utility (scripts/echo.py, docs/echo-usage.md) with zero relation to the job state consistency problem.

The root cause of the inconsistent row (job_20260711T16542651 with status=failed, queue_state=running) is not documented. decision.md makes no mention of queue_state, job_20260711, or the inconsistency.
The known bug in decision_loop/engine.py _clean_stale_state (sets status='expired' without setting queue_state) remains unfixed. No change was made to engine.py.
No consistency check (test or probe) was added to detect mismatched status/queue_state rows.
No SQL reconciliation script was provided for the existing inconsistent row. required_artifact graph-update.yaml is also absent.

integrity.reasoning:
The node job-state-consistency has a clear, well-defined purpose: fix a production bug where jobs.status and jobs.queue_state diverge. The why documents a specific inconsistent row (job_20260711T16542651 at status=failed, queue_state=running) and identifies the culprit (decision_loop/engine.py expiry sets status='expired' only). The acceptance criteria require: (1) root cause documented in decision.md, (2) all write paths set both columns, (3) a consistency check exists, (4) the stale row is reconciled via documented SQL, and (5) tests pass.

What was actually submitted is completely unrelated: artifacts describing implementation of an echo utility (scripts/echo.py, docs/echo-usage.md). The patch.diff shows changes to echo.py and echo documentation — this corresponds to the canary-retry-proof node, not job-state-consistency. The decision.md does not mention queue_state, job_20260711, SQL, or any of the issues this node was meant to address. The engine.py bug (line 59 setting only status='expired' without queue_state='expired') remains untouched. No consistency check exists. No reconciliation SQL was provided. The required graph-update.yaml artifact is absent.

If this work were accepted as satisfying job-state-consistency, the production bug would remain uncorrected, the dashboard would still lie about running counts, and any downstream node that depends on job state consistency would operate on incorrect assumptions. This is a fundamental mismatch between the work delivered and the node's intended role.
